definition: A state of matter with a fixed shape and a fixed volume; it does not flow and is very hard to compress.
A state of matter with a fixed volume but no fixed shape; it flows, takes the shape of the part of its container it fills, and is very hard to compress.
A state of matter with no fixed shape or volume; it flows, spreads out to fill any closed container, and is easily compressed.
The change of state from solid to liquid; a pure substance melts at a fixed temperature, its melting point.
The change of state from liquid to gas that happens all through the liquid, with bubbles of gas forming, at a fixed temperature for a given pressure: the boiling point.
The change of state from gas to liquid, which happens when a gas is cooled enough.
The change from liquid to gas at the surface of a liquid, which can happen below the boiling point; the more energetic particles escape, so the liquid left behind cools.
